story_title: A Shopping Day with Three Choices
paragraphs: On Saturday, Mia goes shopping with her brother Ben. They check the weather before they leave. The forecast says it may rain later. Ben says, "If it {{mask_1}} this afternoon, we {{mask_2}} our umbrellas." Mia checks her shopping list. "If we {{mask_3}} the market before noon, we {{mask_4}} the fresh bread."

At the store, Mia sees a blue jacket she likes, but it costs more than she planned to spend. She says, "If I {{mask_5}} more money, I {{mask_6}} this jacket." Ben points to a cheaper one. "If this jacket {{mask_7}} warm enough, you {{mask_8}} it for the trip."

They remember that they forgot their reusable bags at home. Ben says, "If we {{mask_9}} our bags by the door, we {{mask_10}} them before leaving." Mia laughs and imagines their home with a reminder board. "If we {{mask_11}} a board near the door, we {{mask_12}} forget our bags so often."

At the grocery store, Mia notices that she has left her shopping list at home. She says, "If I {{mask_13}} the list in my phone, I {{mask_14}} every item." Ben looks at the shelf and asks about the last loaf of bread. "If we {{mask_15}} it earlier, we {{mask_16}} it before the other shoppers."

They pay for their things and walk to the bus stop. The next bus is due soon, but the sky is getting dark. Ben says, "If the bus {{mask_17}} on time, we {{mask_18}} home before the rain." Mia smiles. "If we {{mask_19}} everything on our list today, we {{mask_20}} a free afternoon tomorrow." They head home together, carrying their purchases.
